q: Consider the two writ jurisdictions: 1-The Supreme Court's is confined to fundamental rights. 2-A High Court's extends to other legal rights as well. 3-The Supreme Court may decline relief where a fundamental right is shown to be violated. Which is/are correct?
expl: The Supreme Court cannot decline where a fundamental right is violated; a High Court has discretion.
why: The scope is wider in the High Court while the guarantee is stronger in the Supreme Court, and both propositions hold at once.
trapnote: Wider in scope, weaker in guarantee. The two courts differ on both axes in opposite directions.

q: Which writ lies against a private individual?
expl: Habeas corpus is the only writ available against a private person.
why: Each of the other three is directed at a public authority or an inferior tribunal.
trapnote: Illegal detention by anyone may be tested. The other writs presuppose a public office or court.

q: Consider certiorari and prohibition: 1-Prohibition is issued while proceedings are pending. 2-Certiorari quashes an order already made. 3-Both lie only against judicial and not administrative bodies. Which is/are correct?
expl: Certiorari lies against administrative authorities acting judicially as well.
why: The timing distinction is the primary one; the extension to administrative action is the secondary point.
trapnote: Prohibition prevents, certiorari cures. Both may reach administrative bodies acting judicially.

q: On the tenure of the Comptroller and Auditor General, which statement is correct?
options: Five years or until the age of sixty-five, whichever is earlier
Six years or until the age of sixty-five, whichever is earlier
Six years or until the age of sixty-two, whichever is earlier
Six years or until the age of sixty-five, whichever is later
expl: Six years or sixty-five, whichever comes first.
why: The fourth option changes only the final word, which is the least visible variation available.
trapnote: Six and sixty-five, whichever is earlier. Sixty-two is the retirement age for a High Court judge.

q: Consider the Comptroller and Auditor General: 1-He is removed in the manner applicable to a judge of the Supreme Court. 2-He is eligible for further office under the Union after demitting office. 3-His reports are examined by a parliamentary committee. Which is/are correct?
expl: He is barred from further office under the Union or any State.
why: The bar on further office is a post-tenure independence safeguard, distinct from the manner of removal.
trapnote: Two separate safeguards: difficulty of removal during tenure, and a bar on office afterwards.

q: On the strength of the Supreme Court, which statement is correct?
options: The Chief Justice and not more than thirty other judges
The Chief Justice and not more than thirty-three other judges, fixed by the Constitution
The Chief Justice and not more than thirty-three other judges
Not more than thirty-four judges in all, fixed by the Constitution
expl: The number is fixed by Parliament by law, not by the Constitution itself.
why: Two options give the correct arithmetic and attribute it to the wrong source, which is the finer distinction tested.
trapnote: The arithmetic is right in three options. The source of the number is what separates them.

q: On appointment of Supreme Court judges: 1-The collegium rests on interpretation, not express text. 2-An amendment replacing it was struck down in 2015. 3-It fell for violating the separation of powers as such. Correct?
expl: It was struck down for violating the independence of the judiciary, a basic feature.
why: The third statement names a real doctrine but not the ground actually relied on, which is a precise distinction.
trapnote: The ground was judicial independence. Separation of powers is related but was not the stated basis.

q: On the removal of a judge of the Supreme Court, which statement is correct?
options: Proved misbehaviour or incapacity, with a simple majority in both Houses in the same session
Proved misbehaviour or incapacity, with a special majority in both Houses in the same session
Any ground the Houses consider sufficient, with a special majority in both Houses
Proved misbehaviour or incapacity, with a special majority in the lower House alone
expl: The ground is limited and the majority is special, in both Houses in the same session.
why: No judge has ever been removed, the nearest instance having failed in the lower House in 1993.
trapnote: Three elements: limited grounds, special majority, both Houses in the same session.

q: Consider the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court: 1-It extends to disputes between the Union and a State. 2-It extends to disputes between two or more States. 3-It extends to a dispute arising out of a pre-Constitution treaty. Which is/are correct?
expl: Disputes arising out of certain pre-Constitution instruments are expressly excluded.
why: The exclusion is textual and is the limb most often omitted from summaries of this jurisdiction.
trapnote: Federal disputes are covered, with express exclusions for certain pre-Constitution instruments.

q: On the advisory jurisdiction, which statement is correct?
options: The Court must answer, though its opinion does not bind the President
The Court may decline to answer, and its opinion binds the President once given
The Court may decline to answer, and its opinion does not bind the President
The Court must answer, and its opinion binds all courts as a precedent
expl: The Court may decline a reference and the opinion is advisory only.
why: Each wrong option makes one of the two attributes mandatory, so both must be held together.
trapnote: Two attributes: the Court may decline, and the opinion does not bind.

q: Consider public interest litigation: 1-Standing has been relaxed for those unable to approach a court. 2-A letter may be treated as a petition. 3-It is available to agitate a purely private contractual dispute. Which is/are correct?
expl: It is not available for private disputes dressed as public causes.
why: Courts now impose costs where the jurisdiction is invoked for a private or publicity purpose.
trapnote: Relaxed standing does not mean unrestricted standing. Private disputes remain outside.

q: Which statement about the seat of the High Court for Andhra Pradesh is correct?
options: It was established at Amaravati with effect from 2 June 2014
It was established at Amaravati with effect from 1 January 2019
It was established at Vijayawada with effect from 1 January 2019
It continues to be the common High Court at Hyderabad
expl: A separate High Court was constituted at Amaravati from 1 January 2019.
why: The 2014 date is that of bifurcation, when the common High Court continued for a period.
trapnote: Bifurcation in 2014, separate High Court in 2019. The two dates are distinct.

q: Consider the writ of quo warranto: 1-It questions the title of a person to a public office. 2-The office must be of a substantive character. 3-Only a person personally aggrieved may apply. Which is/are correct?
expl: Any member of the public may apply for this writ.
why: The public character of the interest protected explains why standing is open in this one writ.
trapnote: Standing is open here because the interest protected is public, not personal.

q: On the Finance Commission and the body that replaced the Planning Commission, which statement is correct?
options: Both are constitutional bodies established under express provisions
The first rests on a statute and the second on a constitutional provision
The first is a constitutional body and the second rests on a Cabinet resolution
Both rest on Cabinet resolutions, neither having constitutional status
expl: One is constitutional; the other is an executive creation of 2015.
why: This pairing is the standard constitutional-versus-executive trap in the institutional questions.
trapnote: Ask for the source of every body: Constitution, statute, or executive resolution.

q: A magistrate grants remand mechanically without recording reasons. Which statement is correct?
options: The order may be tested only in the Supreme Court, liberty being a fundamental right
The order is not amenable to writ jurisdiction, judicial orders being excluded
The order may be tested only by way of appeal to the Court of Session
The order may be tested in the High Court, whose writ power extends to legal rights
expl: The wider High Court jurisdiction is the appropriate route.
why: The third option states a genuine principle about judicial orders and applies it too broadly.
trapnote: Remand orders are routinely tested. The exclusion of judicial orders is narrower than it sounds.

q: Consider: 1-The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction is itself a fundamental right. 2-A High Court's writ jurisdiction is a fundamental right. 3-The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction may be suspended during an Emergency. Which is/are correct?
expl: The Supreme Court remedy is itself a fundamental right and may be suspended; the High Court's is not a fundamental right.
why: Both correct statements concern the same provision, which is why the middle statement stands out once identified.
trapnote: One remedy is itself a right and is suspendable. The other is a constitutional power, not a right.

q: Which statement about the first public interest litigation concerning undertrial prisoners is correct?
options: It established a speedy trial as part of the guarantee of life and personal liberty
It established free legal aid as an independently enforceable directive
It established the collegium as the method of appointing judges
It established that a letter may never be treated as a petition
expl: Speedy trial and free legal aid were both read into the liberty guarantee.
why: The second option describes the right result by the wrong route, directives not being independently enforceable.
trapnote: Rights were read into the liberty guarantee. Directives were the aid, not the source.

q: Consider the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to a State: 1-They are submitted to the Governor. 2-They are laid before the State legislature. 3-They are examined by the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament. Which is/are correct?
expl: State reports are examined by the State legislature's own committee.
why: The third statement transfers the scrutiny function to the wrong legislature, a straightforward institution swap.
trapnote: Union reports go to Parliament's committee; State reports go to the State committee.

q: On curative petitions, which statement is correct?
options: They lie in place of a review petition where the ground is an error of law
They lie before a review petition is filed, as a preliminary step
They lie only in criminal matters where a death sentence has been confirmed
They lie after a review petition has been dismissed, in rare and exceptional cases
expl: The curative petition is the last resort after dismissal of a review.
why: The fourth option confines a general remedy to a single category of case, which is a common narrowing.
trapnote: Sequence: judgment, review, curative. Each step is narrower than the one before.

q: Consider: 1-The Supreme Court may transfer a case from one High Court to another. 2-A High Court has superintendence over all courts within its territory. 3-A High Court may issue a writ only within its own territorial jurisdiction. Which is/are correct?
expl: A High Court may act where the cause of action arises, even if outside its territory.
why: The territorial extension by reference to the cause of action is the point the third statement suppresses.
trapnote: Territorial jurisdiction is extended by the place where the cause of action arises.
